funder_name: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and partner organisations
funding_summary: Chevening describes the award as fully funded. It covers tuition fees in full, an economy airfare to and from the home country (scholar only), an arrival allowance, the visa application cost (scholar only), a departure allowance, TB testing up to GBP 75 where required, a travel top-up allowance and a monthly living stipend whose amount depends on studying inside or outside London.
summary: One-year master's degrees at UK universities for emerging leaders from Chevening-eligible countries. Applicants need at least two years (or 2,800 hours) of work experience after their undergraduate degree, a degree that qualifies them for a UK master's, and must have finished undergraduate study at least two years before the deadline. They must apply to three different eligible UK courses, hold at least one unconditional offer by the offer deadline, and commit to returning to their country of award for two years after the scholarship. British citizens, people living in the UK, certain government and British Council staff and their relatives, and people who previously studied in the UK on a UK-government scholarship are not eligible; former Chevening Fellows must wait five years. There is no upper age limit. Timeline for this cycle: interviews March to April 2027, results from mid-June 2027, offer deadline 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027, studies from September or October 2027.
deadline_source_text: Applications opened in August 2026 and close in October 2026 at 11:00 UTC; the page says to check your country's page for the exact date. This cycle may already have closed.

funder_name: Erasmus+ programme of the European Union
funding_summary: The page says scholarships cover participation costs and contribute to travel, visa costs and a living allowance, but states no amounts. It also says individual masters may offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide.
summary: International master's programmes delivered jointly by universities in several countries and funded through Erasmus+ grants to the institutions. Open to students from anywhere in the world who hold a bachelor's degree (or an equivalent qualification) or are in their last year and will graduate before the master's starts. Applicants apply directly to the institution running the chosen master's, found through the EU course catalogue, and each master's website explains the steps with and without a scholarship.
route_name: Apply to the individual joint master's programme
deadline_source_text: Each master sets its own deadline; in most cases applications open between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.

funder_name: Republic of Turkiye (Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities)
funding_summary: The page lists support categories: monthly stipend, accommodation, flight ticket, health insurance, language course, adaptation, culture, academy and diploma. Tuition is not explicitly mentioned and no amounts are given.
summary: Turkish government scholarship programme described as competitive and merit-based, with levels from associate degree through bachelor's, master's and PhD, plus short research programmes for international researchers and academics. The scholarship provides financial support and university placement. Applications are submitted online free of charge. The overview page does not list eligibility criteria; confirm them in the current call announcement.
deadline_source_text: The page points to an Application Calendar and a 2026 announcement but gives no dates in the text reviewed; check the calendar page.
